# The Lighthouse Signal

**Built from**: scenes 2026-11-13

<!-- scene:S01 start -->
The wind had been working at the windows since dusk. Maren Holt climbed the last of the stairs with one hand on the rail and the other on her bad left knee, and she did not hurry. Nobody was waiting.

In the lamp room she wiped the glass with her sleeve. Her grey eyes found the dark water the way they had for forty years. The automatic light turned above her, steady and indifferent. She kept the old hand-lamp polished anyway, because someone ought to.

Then the beam stuttered, once, like a held breath.
<!-- scene:S01 end -->
<!-- scene:S01 sha:8cfa0fc0925f8da48de3b4ea4797de669b7c5bc0f8e91bb58169f4b512a32401 -->
<!-- scene:S02 start -->
The clock below struck midnight. She waited for it to happen again. It did: two short flashes, a pause, three long.

I put my palm flat on the cold brass. The mechanism was sound. She knew every gear of it. Nothing in it could make that pattern.

She counted the flashes a third time, and then she stopped pretending it was a fault.
<!-- scene:S02 end -->
<!-- scene:S02 sha:a81e70a2e029ba8160acd92b65196e49399087d4d96dcf8e636131c28ad4a1df -->
<!-- scene:S03 start -->
Boots rang on the iron stairs. "Maren? The harbour radio says your light is acting up."

It was barely seven in the evening, Tobias noted. Tobias Vane came through the hatch breathing hard, rain running off his cap. He was twenty-six and still thought every problem had a toolbox.

"It is not acting up," Maren said, her pale blue eyes steady on the lamp. "Watch."

Two short. A pause. Three long. Tobias stopped smiling, and wondered whether she would ever forgive him for coming; he felt sure she hated visitors.
<!-- scene:S03 end -->
